role: Visitor reading routes through the previously researched Lab model. These labels introduce no definitions, governance axes or relation kinds.

lenses.label: Governance
lenses.question: What governs meaning, evidence and change?
lenses.title: Meaning, evidence and change
lenses.summary: Authority identifies the admitted meaning, contracts, rules and permitted effects within a scope. Provenance traces exact sources and transformations. Lifecycle records independent states and changes through time.
points: Authority: which surfaces govern this subject?
Provenance: where did it come from?
Lifecycle: what is its state, and what changed?
lenses.example: Before an agent changes a customer export, it resolves what “complete” means, traces the input records and checks which actions are permitted.

lenses.label: The Lab model
lenses.question: How do purpose, work and records fit together?
lenses.title: From purpose to implementation
lenses.summary: Intent frames the desired outcome. Products organize durable value; projects coordinate bounded change. Goals, work and implementation connect that purpose to results. Definitions, artifact types and declared relations make the records interpretable.
points: Purpose: intent, products, projects and goals.
Knowledge: typed records and source-bound ontology views.
lenses.example: A product needs reliable data export. A project repairs pagination; its work produces an implementation revision.

lenses.label: Agent work
lenses.question: How does a session act and leave useful knowledge?
lenses.title: A temporary session with durable continuity
lenses.summary: A machine agent is ephemeral. Its assignment, accountability and delegation bound the work it may do. Context and ontology views supply selected project knowledge. Short-term memory belongs to the session; long-term continuity belongs to Project State.
points: Prepare: resolve current context and authority inputs.
Act: perform attributable work within the permitted scope.
Continue: accept useful records for later sessions.
lenses.example: The agent receives a current view, fixes one export boundary and ends its session. Accepted records remain available to the next session.

lenses.label: Operational learning
lenses.question: How can experience improve later work?
lenses.title: Experience that can be examined
lenses.summary: Observations and failure assessments preserve what happened. Research and experiments examine questions. An operational lesson states its evidence, applicability and predicted benefit. Later applications and outcome assessments examine whether that benefit appeared.
points: Observe: preserve an episode and its evidence.
Propose: formulate a bounded, falsifiable lesson.
Assess: examine its use and benefit in later work.
lenses.example: A missed page becomes an observation. A lesson proposes a boundary check; a later application and assessment examine whether the check helped.

lenses.label: Operational scope
lenses.question: What is admitted, implemented or still proposed?
lenses.title: Understand the recorded boundary
lenses.summary: At the 8 October 2026 source snapshot, the Lab has an accepted local runtime implementation and a later accepted project state. The runtime still uses an earlier selection of records. A proposed update selects the later state and requires its own admission. Accepted implementation, observed execution and product readiness each have a distinct scope.
points: Foundation: an accepted implementation with a bounded local scope.
Proposed update: select the later accepted project state.
Roadmap: establish repeatable operation, integration and a stable release.
lenses.example: A candidate successor can have a passing recorded validation receipt and still require its own admission.

lenses.label: Definitions & connections
lenses.question: Where can I inspect the exact model?
lenses.title: Inspect the model’s underlying records
lenses.summary: The reference catalog contains the selected definitions, artifact-type contracts, relation kinds and permitted ordered endpoint pairs. Open a record to inspect its statement, schema binding, admission reference and exact source snapshot.
points: Artifact types: representation contracts and exact bindings.
Relations: declared connections and permitted endpoints.
lenses.example: Find “Ledger,” inspect its admitted definition and follow its exact source.

open_questions: User review of the visual system map and explanation density.
presentation: The six editorial reading lenses remain in the article tree. A prominent conceptual system map adds whole-Lab, governance, purpose/work, agent-session, learning and ontology views with selectable neighborhoods and a guided example.

visual_system_map.relationship: Complementary visual explanation; map views and reading lenses retain their own editorial labels.
